items.title: Modernising threat hunting: Using Semantic Search to Find Risky AI Agent Behavior
items.summary: I tested vector search on 7,454 turns of my own agent sessions. One in seven sessions needed review, the agent’s reasoning carried more signal than the prompt, and the stored vectors answer questions nobody thought to ask at ingest.

items.title: When trust becomes the payload: Inside the threats, etc quarterly report
items.summary: The newest threats, etc report details how adversaries are weaponizing trust across the entire enterprise stack, abusing everything from AI assistants and npm supply chains to identity flows and legitimate management tools.

items.title: Kernel eviction notice: What wesp.sys reveals about the Windows Endpoint Security Platform
items.summary: Microsoft wants EDR out of the Windows kernel, and the preview binaries show wesp.sys telling a user-mode client that a process is starting, with nothing in its imports to let that client block it.

items.title: How CVE-2026-73570 turns a Zimbra log file into remote code execution
items.summary: We reproduced the Zimbra command injection vulnerability and found that several public PoCs write a payload Swatchdog never matches, so a failed test looks like a patched server.

items.title: php2shell: Assessing Elastic detection coverage relevant to CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619
items.summary: CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619 are critical PHP core RCE flaws that leaked ahead of disclosure. We cover what is verified, why exploitation converges on a web server spawning a shell, and the Elastic detections developed to catch this behavior.

items.title: Auditing the auditor: Unmasking Apex Accelerator
items.summary: REF8801 exposes how Apex Accelerator combines convincing Web3 services with malicious npm packages, attacker-controlled AI infrastructure, and cross-platform malware delivery.

items.title: Introducing AlertZero: Inbox zero for your alert queue
items.summary: AlertZero brings AI SOC automation to Elastic Security with four agents, one job each, so the queue stops setting your priorities. Nothing changes in your environment without your approval.

items.title: Behind the tags: How Elastic SIEM grades 1,781 detection rules on noise, speed, and threat coverage
items.summary: This article explains how Elastic SIEM uses a monthly automated telemetry pipeline to score prebuilt detection rules across noise, performance, threat, and profile dimensions, helping security teams decide which rules to enable first.

items.title: No MDM for Linux? A 68-line Elastic workflow keeps every endpoint's config current
items.summary: Elastic InfoSec runs Linux endpoint management through Elastic Defend with a scheduled workflow that gets Cursor and Codex config onto new laptops without piling up duplicate actions on offline hosts, and it works for other config too.

items.title: Quarantined isn't contained: Agentic phishing response with Elastic and Sublime
items.summary: The native Sublime Security integration sends email detections into Elastic Security, where phishing incident response can tie a quarantined email to what happens next on the endpoint and pull the threat from every mailbox it reached.

items.title: Cloud Threat Emulation on Autopilot: Context is Everything
items.summary: Cloud threat emulation is more than detonation. A plan-first methodology for cloud detection engineering: scope, victim model, telemetry, coverage, cleanup. Learn how to properly leverage AI to automate your emulations.

items.title: One SOC, 100 projects: running centralized alert triage on Elastic Security Serverless
items.summary: We linked one Elastic Security project to 100 others and ran the full prebuilt detection catalog from the origin, with all the ingest landing in the linked projects. It held up, and where it deliberately does not reach is the interesting part.

items.title: The extension you never installed: KREMLIN forges Chrome's own integrity checks to steal banking sessions
items.summary: Elastic Security Labs tracked this malicious browser extension across seven campaigns and 15 months, through Brazilian bank lures and the Ethereum smart contracts that hold its C2 configuration.

items.title: Linux Detection Engineering - Local Privilege Escalation
items.summary: Seven of the thirteen Linux privilege escalation CVEs we tracked in 2026 turned out to be the same copy-on-write bug pointed at different kernel interfaces. We ran the public proof-of-concept for eleven exploits and two misconfigurations, and noted which rules fired.

items.title: Why 2026 is the Year to Upgrade to an Agentic AI SOC
items.summary: Agentic AI SOCs differ from copilot-only models by autonomously prioritizing attacks over alerts, executing closed-loop containment, and providing traceable reasoning for every decision, allowing analysts to focus on high-value investigations.

items.title: Data access: the hidden cost of security vendor lock-in
items.summary: Getting data into a security platform is always easy; getting it back out is where vendors add cost, extra tooling, and latency, and it is the part of the evaluation most teams overlook.

items.title: How to correlate Kubernetes audit logs with container runtime data
items.summary: Two fields join the Kubernetes API to what ran inside the pod, and one turns up a container escape your process events never recorded.

items.title: REVSTEALER ramps up: analysis of up-and-coming infostealer
items.summary: Elastic Security Labs deep dives into REVSTEALER, an emerging infostealer targeting browsers, wallets, and gaming accounts.

items.title: Linux Detection Engineering - Fileless Execution
items.summary: We reproduced five Linux fileless execution patterns with FENIX, including memfd_create staging, interpreter one-liners, deleted binaries, and in-memory kernel module loads, then mapped each to the Elastic Defend rules that catch it.

items.title: From 88 lines to 1: Detecting DLL hijacking with Elastic Defend
items.summary: The ClickFix campaign that sideloads a malicious mscoree.dll also ships a driver to kill Elastic Endpoint. We rebuilt that DLL as a NativeAOT library, dropped it beside a signed Microsoft binary, and Elastic Defend 9.5.0 flagged the load.

items.title: Inside Elastic's agentic SOC: How we took AI alert triage from 60% to 92% accuracy
items.summary: Elastic's InfoSec team runs three agents that read the detection rule's investigation guide and the closure reasons on 30 days of past cases. Analysts now clear most alerts with a single click in Slack.

items.title: How a team of entity maintainers monitors, connects and scores entities in Elastic Security
items.summary: Inside Elastic Security, background jobs called maintainers each own one piece of every user, host and service record, from building entities out of raw logs to resolving identities and scoring risk.

items.title: 13 million tool calls: auditing every AI coding agent action with Elastic Agent
items.summary: Cursor hooks and Elastic Agent capture every tool call, shell command, file read and MCP request as structured events you can hunt with ES|QL.

items.title: The security signal log tailing can't see: tracking npm cooldown removals with Elastic Agent
items.summary: A 40-line CEL integration snapshots .npmrc files every 6 hours to catch cooldown removals. This post walks through the three ways we broke filestream before landing on snapshot semantics.

items.title: Living off the coding agent: Two tales of tunnels and LaunchAgents
items.summary: Agent-parented reverse tunnels and LaunchAgents can expose a local admin app to the internet. Endpoint still needs to treat that as high severity even when the activity looks like vibe-coded ops, not confirmed malware.

items.title: Shai-Hulud strikes again: CHAINDROP worm hits 400+ npm packages
items.summary: Elastic Security Labs identified the return of Shai-Hulud. Attackers compromised the keyv maintainer and deployed CHAINDROP, a worm that uses stolen npm credentials to backdoor co-owned packages totaling over 1.3 billion monthly downloads.

items.title: Benchmarking the Agentic SOC: How we evaluate LLMs for security workflows
items.summary: Public leaderboards can't tell you which LLM to trust in your SOC, so Elastic built an evaluation framework that grades models on the work (tool calls, execution traces, blind judging) across Agent Builder, Attack Discovery, and automatic migration.

items.title: Agents vs. agents: how we triage HackerOne reports for $2 each, 85% as well as a human
items.summary: LLMs made it cheap to flood bug bounty programs with submissions. Here's how Elastic built an AI triage agent that matches human decisions 85% of the time, including the architecture, threat model and calibration against 3,300 real reports

items.title: SOC case management and detection rule history in Elastic Security
items.summary: Elastic Security now tracks every detection rule change with one-click rollback and makes case data queryable out of the box, so SOC teams get audit trails and reporting without configuring anything.

items.title: Elastic goes all-in on Hacker Summer Camp at Black Hat and DEF CON in Las Vegas
items.summary: Attack Discovery turns raw alerts into validated threats and Elastic Defend closes vulnerable driver gaps as fast as they're disclosed. Watch it all run against real attacks at the booth.
